newsitem.title: USA: Rohm and Haas says Q2 margins best since '88.
newsitem.headline: Rohm and Haas says Q2 margins best since '88.

text.p: Rohm and Haas Co said Thursday it achieved record sales and earnings growth and the strongest profit margins since 1988 as its acrylic and electronic chemicals units performed strongly.
The company reported second quarter earnings of $115 million or $1.85 per share, compared with $99 million or $1.50 a share in the second quarter of 1996.
The company said the per-share increase reflects the impact of the company's repurchase of six percent of its common shares since the end of June 1996.

"Rohm and Haas achieved record levels of sales and earnings growth," said chairman J. Lawrence Wilson, "and profit margins were the best they've been since the second quarter of 1988." Both selling prices and raw material costs were down slightly from year-ago levels.
Sales of $1.09 billion were three percent ahead of the $1.05 billion reported for the second quarter of 1996 on unit volume that was up 10 percent over the previous year.
Sales were up seven percent after adjustments for the formation of a joint venture and discontinued businesses.
The company's acrylic and electronic chemicals businesses contributed heavily to the profit improvement.

Unit volume for the acrylic businesses (Polymers and Resins, Monomers, Formulation Chemicals, Plastics Additives and AtoHaas Americas) was 15 percent higher overall than the year before, the company said.

Fast- rowing demand led to outstanding sales and earnings growth for Shipley Co the primary segment of the Electronic Chemicals business. Overall earnings were helped by the elimination of losses associated with AtoHaas Europe, excellent manufacturing operations and a strong performance by the Latin American region, it said.
Rohm said weaker foreign currencies reduced per common share earnings by $0.19.
Both the European and Asia-Pacific regions reported lower earnings as a result of seven percent weaker European currencies and a 13 percent weaker Japanese yen.
The Agricultural Chemicals business also reported lower earnings, due to poor weather conditions and the lack of pest pressure in key markets.
In the second quarter of 1996, Rohm and Haas recorded a $10 million, or $0.15 per common share retroactive tax credit.
